Metadata.title: Ibrik Kitchen — Balkan Kitchen, Paris Sentier
Metadata.description: A Balkan kitchen in the Sentier, Paris 2. Romanian, Greek, Serbian and Turkish classics meet French bistronomy. The Balkans are home to everyone.

Hero.blurb: A loud, warm Balkan kitchen in the Sentier. Slow food from the Carpathians to the Aegean, from somebody's bunică's back garden — cooked the way it has always been cooked.
Hero.takeaway: Eat in or take away · la pachet

About.title:
A kitchen
remembered
by hand.
About.p1: Ibrik began with Ecaterina — a tax lawyer from Bucharest who arrived in Paris at six, then quit law to cook the food she'd missed. Ibrik Café opened in 2018; Ibrik Kitchen, in the heart of the Sentier, followed in 2019.
About.p2: Her recipes travel from the Carpathians to the Aegean — sarmale, mititei and cevapcici, souvlaki, halloumi, papanași — cooked by award-winning chefs with one quiet idea: the Balkans are home to everyone.

Menu.lead: A taste of the carte — mezze, embers, slow-cooked, and sweets. Order three plates between two. Stay for coffee.

Press.title:
They keep
coming back.
Press.q1: The sarmale is a love letter written in cabbage and smoke. We did not stop eating.
Press.q2: An act of memory. Ibrik makes a Bucharest grandmother's table feel inevitable, even necessary.
Press.q3: A papanași so tender it briefly cured a hangover and a heartbreak in the same bite.

Events.p1: There is a Romanian word — petrecere — that means a party, a feast, and the act of "passing time" all at once. We were built for it.
Events.p2: Whether it's twelve around the long table or sixty taking the whole room, we cook the way our families cook for theirs: too much, all at once, and so good that nobody quite leaves on time.
Events.card1Meta: 12–24 guests · whole back room · 3 courses, family style
Events.card2Meta: Up to 60 guests · full restaurant · custom menu with the kitchen
Events.card3Meta: Catering off-site · sarmale by the hundred · țuică by the case

Reserve.lead: Everyone is welcome — people often assume the room is full when it isn't. Just ask, we'll find you a table.
Reserve.takeawayText: Eating at home tonight? The whole menu is also available to take away — drop by or give us a call to order.
Reserve.asideP1: Looks busy? It often does — there's almost always room for one more. Call without hesitating.
Reserve.asideP2: Large parties, last-minute, surprise birthdays: tell us and we'll make it work.

Video.lead: Our chef Cathy welcomes McFly & Carlito and Cyprien into the Ibrik kitchen and walks them through the gestures — sarmale, mămăligă, papanași. An hour of Romanian petrecere, the way it happens at home.

Faq.title:
Your questions,
answered.
Faq.lead: Address, opening hours, bookings, vegetarian dishes and what to order — the things people ask us most.

where.a: Ibrik Kitchen is at 9 rue de Mulhouse, 75002 Paris, in the Sentier district. It is a two-minute walk from Sentier metro station (line 3) and five minutes from Bonne Nouvelle (lines 8 and 9) and Réaumur — Sébastopol (lines 3 and 4). Phone: +33 1 70 69 42 50.

hours.q: What are Ibrik Kitchen's opening hours?
hours.a: Ibrik Kitchen is open Monday to Saturday: lunch from 12:00 to 15:30, dinner from 19:00 to 00:30. The restaurant is closed on Sundays.

cuisine.q: What kind of food does Ibrik Kitchen serve?
cuisine.a: Ibrik Kitchen serves Balkan food — Romanian, Greek, Serbian and Turkish — cooked with French bistronomy technique. The signature dishes are sarmale (cabbage leaves stuffed with Angus beef), mititei grilled over embers, chicken souvlaki, lamb shoulder marinated and cooked for seven hours, and papanași for dessert.

booking.q: Do I need to book a table at Ibrik?
booking.a: Booking is recommended, especially for dinner and on Saturdays. You can book online through Zenchef, by phone on +33 1 70 69 42 50, or by email at bureau@ibrik.fr. The room often looks full when it is not — call us, there is nearly always a table left.

vegetarian.q: Are there vegetarian dishes on the menu?
vegetarian.a: Yes, at every service. Mezze: barbecue-smoked aubergine caviar, feta roasted with honey and hazelnuts, courgette fritter with feta, fennel risoni. Mains: pepper stuffed with pilaf rice, BLKN Avo' Toast, and souvlaki in a vegetarian version with feta. Vegetarian dishes are marked with a V on the menu.

budget.q: How much does a meal cost?
budget.a: At lunch, set menus run from €25 (mezze + main, or main + dessert) to €33 (mezze + main + dessert). At dinner, à la carte: mezze €11 to €17, mains €14 to €33, desserts €11 to €14. Expect €40 to €55 per person, before drinks.

groups.q: Can we come as a group or hire the whole restaurant?
groups.a: Yes. The big table — masa mare — seats 12 to 24 guests from €58 per person, served family-style across three courses. The whole restaurant can be hired for up to 60 people from €4,200. Ibrik also caters christenings and weddings. Write to bureau@ibrik.fr or call +33 1 70 69 42 50.

chef.a: Ecaterina, known to everyone as Cathy. Born in Bucharest, in Paris since she was six, a former doctor of tax law who left it all to cook what she missed. She opened Ibrik Café in 2018, then Ibrik Kitchen in the Sentier in 2019. The kitchen is run by a brigade of award-winning chefs.

order.q: What should I order on a first visit?
order.a: Three dishes for two, shared. Start with the smoked aubergine caviar and the roasted feta, move on to the sarmale or the mititei straight off the embers, and finish with the pistachio cake — the house best-seller — and an IBRIK coffee brewed Balkan-style, which takes 5 to 10 minutes.
